The core stayed compact across the original run. Radius of gyration measures how widely selected backbone atoms spread around their center; it does not mean the structure stayed unchanged. Original plot: core Cα, residue IDs 3–15 on PEPA–D, stride 10. The horizontal axis is saved frame, not verified nanoseconds.

The predefined guanine contacts did not remain consistently short. These distance checks do not show a persistent quartet, and they do not prove a quartet formed and then fell apart. Original distance axes are in angstroms and the horizontal axes show saved frame indices.

Built-in Fe–His distances fluctuate near 2.11 Å. This checks an imposed coordination site; it does not demonstrate spontaneous hemin binding. The original plots use saved frame indices; a physical nanosecond interval is not verified.
Early guanosine-linked monomer, shown after the custom amide connection was added. This direct-link prototype predates the mixed His/Ala PEG2 model.
An early manually placed heme model with one Fe–His distance of 2.150 Å. This was a geometry test, distinct from the later A/C bis-His PEG2 model.
Four early nucleopeptide chains arranged as a starting bundle. The geometry was constructed; the image does not show observed self-assembly.
The early all-His pocket. Yellow measurements show neighboring histidine nitrogen separations of 4.387 Å before heme placement. This is an earlier design, not the mixed His/Ala PEG2 reference.
